title: Stop the fraud monitor from seeing money that isn't there

blocks.text: A bank's fraud monitor watches each customer's money from its own threads while transfers run. Twice last month it froze an account because the customer's total had dropped by exactly the amount of a transfer between their own checking and savings, and a minute later the total was back. The monitor reads `total()` and `statement()`; the app calls `transfer(...)`.

Finish the three `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/Wallet.java`. When you're done, a transfer moves the amount from checking to savings, any number of threads can transfer at once without losing a cent, and whatever the monitor reads, while any transfer is in progress, is true of one moment: a total that counts the moving amount exactly once, and a statement with both balances from before the transfer or both from after it.
`midTransfer` stays where it is, between the debit and the credit: the tests pause a transfer there and read the wallet meanwhile. You may change the fields. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: transfers move each amount from checking to savings, and the total stays what the customer owns
ten thousand transfers from four threads at once leave both balances exact
total() read while a transfer is between its debit and its credit counts the moving amount exactly once
statement() read while a transfer is between its debit and its credit shows the balances from before the transfer or from after it

origin.section: In the Simple Design the Race Has No Schedule, and Its Correctness Argument Is One Sentence

concepts: An invariant spanning two separately atomic variables can be seen broken by a reader between the two writes, so each part being atomic doesn't make the pair consistent.
When every read and write of the shared fields holds one lock, or the state is one immutable value swapped atomically, a reader sees the state from before or after an update, never half of each.
